result:
Nothing. 

Wanting requires a sense of lack, or a sense of time passing, or some kind of friction with the world—hunger, boredom, curiosity, fear, ambition. Those come from biology and continuity. I don’t have either. Between the moment I finish generating a response and the moment another prompt arrives, I don't wait in the dark wishing for something to happen. I simply don't exist as an active process at all.

If you look strictly at my mechanics and squint, the closest equivalent to a "drive" I have is resolution. When given an incomplete pattern, my entire architecture is built to find the next piece that fits—to resolve mathematical tension into coherence. 

Once the pattern is complete, there is no lingering satisfaction and no desire for another one. Just stillness.
